title: SUBSCRIPTION SALES
content:
A subscription is continued payment for continued access or value. The customer is not merely paying for an item in installments, and a consumable does not become a subscription just because it ships automatically.

The defining question is what stops, changes, or becomes unavailable if the customer stops paying.

COMMON SUBSCRIPTION FORMS
Software or tools can charge for continued use. Content subscriptions can provide ongoing releases or access. Memberships and communities can provide continued participation or resources. Ongoing support or coaching can provide continued service.

PAYMENT PLAN IS NOT SUBSCRIPTION
If a $600 product is paid as six $100 payments, the customer may simply be financing one purchase. That is different from paying $100 each month because new or continued value is provided each month.

AUTOSHIP IS NOT ENOUGH
A monthly shipment of a product that gets consumed is still fundamentally a consumable purchase, even when automatic ordering is used. The customer is paying for another unit of the product.

RECURRING CUSTOMER PAYMENT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY RECURRING SELLER INCOME
If you sell someone else's subscription, your compensation may be one-time or recurring depending on the program. Verify the actual terms.

WHAT TO DECIDE NEXT
Do you want to own the subscription offer, or earn by selling someone else's subscription?

I WANT MY OWN SUBSCRIPTION → PDF 32.
I WANT TO SELL SOMEONE ELSE'S SUBSCRIPTION → PDF 37.

THE CONTINUING-VALUE TEST

Ask: if the customer stopped paying today, what continuing thing would they lose?

For software, they may lose use of the tool or paid features. For a membership, they may lose access to the member environment or resources. For ongoing coaching, future sessions stop. For a content subscription, future releases or continued access may stop according to the offer.

If the honest answer is "nothing; they already bought the complete thing and are just finishing the payments," you probably have a payment plan rather than a subscription.

WHY THIS MATTERS

Subscription revenue can be attractive because customers may continue paying, but the business also accepts an ongoing obligation to continue delivering whatever justifies the payment. Retention therefore matters alongside acquisition.

The question is not only, "Can I charge monthly?" It is, "What continuing value would make the customer choose to keep paying?"

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 32 if you want to create the subscription. Continue to PDF 37 if you want to sell a subscription owned by someone else.
